sentences.text:
Durgesh Dhurve vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 October,
2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Jbp:50468
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal

On The 7 th Of October, 2025
 Misc. Criminal Case No. 33754 of 2025
 Durgesh Dhurve
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Ravinandan Dwivedi - Advocate for applicant.
Shri Pradeep Gupta - Government Advocate for State.

Order 
This is third application under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of bail filed on behalf of the applicant who has been arrested relating to Crime No.153/2023 registered at Police Station Sirali, District Harda, for offences punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376(3), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 3/4,
5(l)/6 of the POCSO Act.
Applicant is in detention since 27.07.2023.

His first bail application was dismissed on merit on 25.10.2023 in M.Cr.C. No.46373/2023.
2.
Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent.
He has been falsely implicated.
He is in custody since 27.07.2023.
It is further submitted that statements of prosecutrix and her mother have been recorded in which they have not supported the prosecution story.
It is further submitted that age of the prosecutrix is about 21 years.

He has placed reliance upon the decision of this Court in the case of Prince Chouhan Vs. NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-JBP:50468 2 MCRC-33754-2025 State of M.P. and other passed in Cr.A.
No.12540/2023 .

sentences.text: The trial will take considerable time to conclude.
Upon these grounds, it is prayed that the applicant be released on bail.

3. On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application and prayed for its rejection by submitting that at the time of incident, age of the prosecutrix was about 15 years.
Present applicant has committed rape with the minor prosecutrix.
DNA is positive.
It is further submitted that at this stage, minute appreciation of evidence cannot be done.

In this regard, he has placed reliance upon the decision of Apex Court in the case of Satish Jaggi Vs. State of Chhattisgarh,
(2007) 11 SCC 195 .

5. Having taken in to consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case and looking to the seriousness of offence, this Court does not find it fit to release the applicant on bail.
6. Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands dismissed.
